findings.trigger: OpenSSL QUIC automatic connected-UDP peer address detection
evidence: Actual JDK21 HttpClient supports HTTP_1_1/HTTP_2, not HTTP/3/QUIC
Default SunJSSE, JDK Lettuce TLS and PG driver factory observed; no native OpenSSL JNI bridge among full 97 JARs/all 26717 entry headers
Native OpenSSL QUIC entrypoint exists in dormant general-purpose openssl CLI, but Java entrypoint and 61 business classes do not spawn it

findings.trigger: OpenSSL QUIC client processing retransmitted CRYPTO frames
evidence: Affected implementation is specifically OpenSSL QUIC, not generic TLS client operation
The exact configured service uses JDK TLS providers; real Java HTTPS over loopback negotiated TLSv1.3 without loading libssl/libcrypto
No business process execution or native library loading method reference; generic CLI override is outside this disposition

findings.trigger: OpenSSL AES-GCM-SIV incremental AAD sequence containing zero-length update
evidence: Actual provider for tested AES/GCM/NoPadding is SunJCE and its real roundtrip passed
AES/GCM-SIV/NoPadding has no available provider in this exact runtime
No OpenSSL libcrypto loaded by actual Java TLS/Redis/PG initialization, so this OpenSSL SIV AAD-update implementation is not reached

findings.trigger: OpenSSL AES-GCM-SIV initialized through EVP_CipherInit_ex with non-12-byte IV
evidence: Exact Java runtime does not offer AES/GCM-SIV and does not load the affected OpenSSL implementation
The real JDK TLS handshake used TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, not GCM-SIV
This is an implementation/path distinction, not an assertion that arbitrary supplied IVs would be safe in system openssl

findings.trigger: OpenSSL CMS_encrypt/_ex with attacker-controlled EC group-order1 recipient certificate
evidence: Actual business classes have no openssl subprocess, Runtime.exec or System.load references, and no CMS encryption entrypoint
Actual PG and Lettuce factories and Java TLS use JDK providers; OpenSSL advisory explicitly separates the CMS-encrypt condition from TLS/QUIC
System openssl CLI imports CMS_encrypt_ex and remains vulnerable for manual CMS use; its presence is recorded, not erased
Inherited CA helper only invokes openssl x509 for certificate metadata/fingerprint and is not the final Java entrypoint

Manual use of openssl CMS/QUIC/GCM-SIV commands or other workflows outside the current Java service
boundary: Affected OpenSSL utilities/libraries remain installed and unpatched. These five technical dispositions cover only this exact configured Java workload. They do not certify all utilities, arbitrary future configuration, production security or model behavior.
